    Key Catalog

    Open Tools > UI Navigation > Key Catalog to manage the addresses shared by UXML, Navigation Graphs, and runtime signals. The catalog is an authoring registry: it keeps references consistent, but it does not create views or perform navigation by itself.

    Address rules

    Every address is a Category / Key pair. Leading and trailing whitespace is removed, and matching is case-sensitive. For example, Demo / Home and demo / Home are different addresses.

    The catalog separates addresses into three tabs:

    Tab Register here when the address is used by
    View NavElement, UI node Show/Hide commands, and UI View outputs
    Button NavButton, NavToggle, UI Button and Toggle outputs, and matching Portal conditions
    Signal UINavigationEvents.RequestSignal, Signal outputs, and matching Portal conditions
    Note

    NavButton exposes signal-category and signal-key in UXML, but its address belongs to the Button catalog because it emits a button signal.

    Create and assign an address

    1. Select the View, Button, or Signal tab.
    2. Add a Category, then add one or more Keys to it.
    3. Select that address from the picker in UI Builder or a Navigation Graph Inspector.

    The Getting started example registers these addresses before assigning them:

    • View: Demo / Home, Demo / Settings
    • Button: Demo / OpenSettings

    Registering an address first avoids free-form spelling differences between UXML and the graph.

    Scan Project and Refresh Usage

    Scan Project examines every UXML VisualTreeAsset and .uinavgraph in the project. It finds addresses used by NavElement, NavButton, NavToggle, UI node View commands and outputs, and Portal conditions, then adds missing entries to the appropriate tab.

    Refresh Usage rescans the same supported assets and updates usage counts without changing the catalog. Select a Key to inspect the asset path and context of each reference.

    Project scanning does not parse C# string literals, custom serialized fields, or application-specific address formats. Add addresses that exist only in code manually.

    Rename and delete safely

    Renaming a Category or Key shows the affected UXML and graph assets before applying the change. After confirmation, the catalog updates supported references together. If an update fails, modified source files are restored from their in-memory backups.

    Deleting behaves differently: it removes only the catalog entry. Existing UXML and graph strings remain and are shown as unregistered references. Running Scan Project later registers them again, so rename the address when the intent is to migrate existing usages.

    Storage and version control

    The catalog is stored at ProjectSettings/UITKNavigationKeyCatalog.asset. Commit this file with the UXML and graph assets that use it so the team shares the same address list. It is an Editor-only authoring asset and is not included in player builds; runtime matching uses the serialized Category / Key values.
